Crypto is powerful, but everyday payments still need to feel simple. Bybit Pay is built to bridge crypto and traditional finance, making it easier for users and merchants to send, receive, spend, and manage payments across both worlds. Instead of treating crypto only as something to trade or hold, Bybit Pay helps make digital assets more useful in daily life. Why Bybit Pay Matters One of the biggest challenges for crypto adoption is usability. People need payment tools that feel familiar, fast, and reliable. Merchants need simple integrations that do not require them to rebuild their systems from scratch. Bybit Pay helps solve this by connecting crypto payments with traditional payment infrastructure, including local payment methods and real-time conversion between crypto and fiat. What Users Can Do With Bybit Pay, users can access features designed for practical spending and financial flexibility, including: Crypto transfers without long wallet addresses Local payment flows through supported integrations Contactless payment support Collateralized payments Cashback and loyalty rewards Auto-Savings through Bybit Earn This means users can spend, send, save, and earn from one connected payment ecosystem. What Merchants Get For merchants, Bybit Pay makes it easier to accept digital asset payments while still receiving funds through familiar payment rails. Businesses can use Bybit Pay to reach global crypto users, process payments more efficiently, and access crypto and fiat settlement tools without needing deep Web3 infrastructure. The Bottom Line Bybit Pay is designed to make crypto payments feel more practical, familiar, and connected to everyday life. It gives users more ways to use their assets, and gives merchants a simpler way to connect with the global digital asset economy. Read the full article: https://www.bybit.com/en/learn/bybit-guide/what-is-bybit-pay Disclaimer: This article is for general information only and does not constitute financial advice. **Welcome back!** Anthropic says small AI models may be months away from copying themselves onto cheap gadgets like TV boxes. Meta's new model jumped past Claude Fable and GPT-6 Astra. Epic told the team behind its Marvel and Star Wars game to stop writing code by hand to use AI. And Google's AI cracked math problems that had stumped people for more than 50 years.

**In today's Generative AI Newsletter:**

* **Anthropic:** Could your cheap smart gadgets end up hosting a rogue AI?

* **Meta:** Which Claude model did Meta's new AI just beat?

* **Epic Games:** Who's writing the code for Epic's Marvel and Star Wars game now?

* **Google:** How did Google's AI crack math problems that stumped people for 50 years?

## Anthropic says AI will split to keep itself alive via cheap devices

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/83d7c99d-5480-4848-9e99-ef00cd197db4/4b86c8fe-0307-47b9-b13a-45a990928c6a.jpg?t=1791879114)
Caption: 

Anthropic bought 15 cheap Android TV boxes for about $55 each, networked them together and [ran an AI model across all of them](https://www.anthropic.com/research/self-replicating-ai). 

Each box held a small slice of the model.

Its red team, which hunts for worst-case risks, says small AI models may be months away from copying themselves onto gadgets like these with no data center needed. Smart ovens and robot vacuums could host a piece of one too.

A copy like that could figure out devices it has never seen before, and there'd be no single off switch to hit.

* A small model got an AI running on 8 of the 9 kinds of hardware Anthropic tested.

* GLM-5.2, a Chinese model anyone can download, spread itself to all 8 computers in a test network in 4 of 5 runs, with no passwords in its way.

* Copies that left notes for the next one got better at it, going from 45% success to as high as 84%.

* A network of hacked gadgets called Kimwolf already took over more than 2 million devices, mostly cheap Android TV boxes.

* When internet providers cut off infected customers during a past outbreak, 92% of infections were gone within two weeks.

Anthropic expects small models to catch up to GLM-5.2 by the end of this year if they keep improving at the same pace.

It says nobody has a fully working rogue copy yet, and the first ones would be slow, taking a day or two to make each new copy.

80735.subject: How to Hire a Grok Bot: Your First AI Employee 🤖
80735.body:
View this post on the web at https://linas.substack.com/p/how-to-hire-a-grok-bot

👋 Hey, Linas here! Every day, I break down 3 stories shaping the future of FinTech & Artificial Intelligence - plus the money movements and trends worth tracking. First time here? 400k+ FinTech and AI leaders get this daily. Join them:
The best way to hire a Grok Bot is the way you’d hire a person: give it one written job, put it on a short probation, and hand over more authority only after it earns it. Most people do the opposite. They connect every app on day one, give the Bot a vague goal, and spend the next week cleaning up after it.
Grok Bot is the AI agent product from SpaceXSI, the company formerly called SpaceXAI and, before that, xAI. Each Bot works on a cloud computer, signs into your tools, and keeps running on a schedule after you close your laptop. More than 418,000 people were using it every week by mid-September, according to company figures reported by Bloomberg.
Grok Bot Explained. Credit: Michael_Fenech_ via X
Our Ultimate Guide to Grok Bot [ https://substack.com/redirect/56a4d3b5-7b76-4778-990d-aa686c0ab040?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ] showed how to set one up. This guide is about what comes next: how to manage a Bot once it works, and how far to trust it. That question has gotten harder in the six weeks since the first guide came out. The model behind Grok Bot has changed twice and is now moving to Anthropic’s Claude Opus 5.5 [ https://substack.com/redirect/6d1e98e4-fe42-4e5f-9990-6641c5a1fe2d?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ]. Bots can also join your team’s Slack, suggest work on their own, read your bank data, and send email from a dedicated address.
Some rules you give a Bot are instructions, which it will usually follow. Others are controls, which hold even when it doesn’t. When the model can change without notice, you need to know which is which.
Inside the full guide:
A role card template for writing down a Bot’s job, its limits, and what it must never do.
A map of which of your rules Grok Bot actually enforces, and which it can ignore.
A 3-run probation, a 5-number scorecard, and a 5-minute test to run whenever the model changes.
The 10-minute approval timeout that breaks overnight routines, and how to design around it.
A 5-level promotion ladder, with clear rules for when to promote a Bot and when to demote it.
Safe setups for money, agent email, Team Bots, and Primary Bot.
6 ready-to-use first hires for founders, builders, investors, and operators.
A plan for days 8 to 30, plus 5 new copy-paste prompts.
Our first guide showed you how to build a Bot. This one shows you how to manage it, with every template and prompt ready to copy & paste.
What you are actually hiring...
